script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

JANE (mid 40s, disheveled, with bags under her eyes) pours herself a cup of coffee. She winces as steam rises from the mug.

JANE
(sighs)
Another day.

Suddenly, the door opens, and her TEN-YEAR-OLD SON, MARK, bursts in, wearing a sheepish expression.

MARK
Mom, I'm late for school. Can you make me a sandwich?

Jane looks at him with frustration.

JANE
(angrily)
You're always late! Why can't you make your own sandwich?

MARK
(apologetically)
I'm sorry, Mom. I'll make it up to you.

Jane rolls her eyes.

JANE
I don't want apologies. I want responsibility.

Mark looks down, his shoulders slumping.

MARK
(whispers)
I know. I'll try harder.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane sits on the couch, staring blankly at the television. Her husband, MIKE (late 40s, tired-looking), enters the room.

MIKE
(sadly)
Another long day?

JANE
(bitterly)
Yes. And I had to deal with Mark being late again.

Mike sits next to her.

MIKE
(softly)
Jane, you're not alone in this. We both carry the weight of our responsibilities.

JANE
(tearfully)
I know, but it feels like I'm drowning.

MIKE
(reassuringly)
We'll get through this. Together.

INT. CLASSROOM - DAY

Mark sits in class, distracted. The TEACHER, MS. JONES (early 30s, kind), approaches him.

MS. JONES
(smiling)
Mark, I noticed you seem distracted today. Is everything okay at home?

MARK
(shrugs)
It's the same old stuff.

MS. JONES
(concerned)
Well, if you ever need someone to talk to, I'm here for you.

INT. JANE'S OFFICE - DAY

Jane sits at her desk, staring at a pile of papers. Her boss, MR. GARCIA (late 50s, stern), enters the room.

MR. GARCIA
(frustrated)
Jane, these reports are overdue. Why haven't you finished them?

JANE
(apologetic)
I've been dealing with personal issues.

MR. GARCIA
(skeptical)
Your personal issues can't keep you from doing your job. I expect these reports on my desk by the end of the day.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jane stands at the sink, washing dishes. Mike enters the room and puts his arms around her.

MIKE
(softly)
You're doing the best you can. I believe in you.

JANE
(tearfully)
But it's not enough. I feel like I'm letting everyone down.

MIKE
(reassuringly)
You're not letting anyone down. We all have our struggles. But we can overcome them, together.

INT. CLASSROOM - DAY

Mark raises his hand in class.

MS. JONES
(smiling)
Yes, Mark?

MARK
(confidently)
I'd like to help clean the classroom today.

MS. JONES
(impressed)
Wonderful! I know you'll do a great job.

INT. JANE'S OFFICE - DAY

Jane sits at her desk, determined. She types furiously on her computer, focusing on her work.

MR. GARCIA
(surprised)
Jane, these reports are impressive.

JANE
(smiling)
Thank you, Mr. Garcia. I had some help.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jane and Mike sit at the table, enjoying a quiet dinner.

MARK
(smiling)
Mom, Dad, I'm sorry for being late so often. I'll make sure it doesn't happen again.

JANE
(smiling back)
We understand, Mark. What's important is that you're learning from your mistakes.

MIKE
(proudly)
Yes, and you're doing a great job, Jane. Keep up the good work.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane and Mike cuddle on the couch, watching a movie. Mark joins them, resting his head on Jane's lap.

MARK
(contentedly)
I'm glad we're all here, together.

JANE
(smiling)
Me too, Mark. Me too.

FADE OUT.
